arxiv-2010-14110.title: Full-Duplex Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems: Analysis and Decentralized Optimization Thanks: Date of submission: 22 November, 2021. Part of this work was published in IEEE ICC 2021. The conference details are as follows: S. Datta, E. Sharma, D. N. Amudala, R. Budhiraja and S. S. Panwar, “FD Cell-Free
arxiv-2010-14110.creator: Soumyadeep Datta, Dheeraj Naidu Amudala, Ekant Sharma, Rohit Budhiraja
arxiv-2010-14110.description: Abstract Cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input-multiple-output (mMIMO) deployments are usually investigated with half-duplex nodes and high-capacity fronthaul links. To leverage the possible gains in throughput and energy efficiency (EE) of full-duplex (FD) communications, we consider a FD CF mMIMO system with practical limited-capacity fronthaul links .

arxiv-2203-04625.title: VECTOR-SPREAD MONOMIAL IDEALS AND ELIAHOU–KERVAIRE TYPE RESOLUTIONS
arxiv-2203-04625.creator: Antonino Ficarra
arxiv-2203-04625.description: Abstract We introduce the class of vector-spread monomial ideals. This notion generalizes that of t t -spread ideals introduced by Ene, Herzog and Qureshi. In particular, we focus on vector-spread strongly stable ideals, we compute their Koszul cycles and describe their minimal free resolution. As a consequence the graded Betti numbers and the Poincaré series are determined.

arxiv-2210-16701.title: Generalized network density matrices for analysis of multiscale functional diversity
arxiv-2210-16701.creator: Arsham Ghavasieh, Manlio De Domenico
arxiv-2210-16701.description: Abstract The network density matrix formalism allows for describing the dynamics of information on top of complex structures and it has been successfully used to analyze from system’s robustness to perturbations to coarse graining multilayer networks from characterizing emergent network states to performing multiscale analysis. However, this framework is usually limited to diffusion dynamics on undirected networks.

arxiv-2408-06352.title: Using Large Language Models to Compare Explainable Models for Smart Home Human Activity Recognition Conference: Companion of the 2024 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing ; October 5–9, 2024; Melbourne, VIC, Australia Companion of the 2024 ACM International Joint
arxiv-2408-06352.creator: Michele Fiori, Gabriele Civitarese, Claudio Bettini
arxiv-2408-06352.description: Abstract . Recognizing daily activities with unobtrusive sensors in smart environments enables various healthcare applications. Monitoring how subjects perform activities at home and their changes over time can reveal early symptoms of health issues, such as cognitive decline. Most approaches in this field use deep learning models, which are often seen as black boxes mapping sensor data to activities.

arxiv-2410-01440.title: Closed-loop Long-horizon Robotic Planning via Equilibrium Sequence Modeling
arxiv-2410-01440.creator: Jinghan Li, Zhicheng Sun, Yadong Mu
arxiv-2410-01440.description: Abstract In the endeavor to make autonomous robots take actions, task planning is a major challenge that requires translating high-level task descriptions to long-horizon action sequences. Despite recent advances in language model agents, they remain prone to planning errors and limited in their ability to plan ahead.

arxiv-2506-17133.title: Robust Training with Data Augmentation for Medical Imaging Classification Thanks: This paper was accepted to the 9 th 9^{\text{th}} International Workshop on Health Intelligence (W3PHIAI-25) at AAAI 2025.
arxiv-2506-17133.creator: Josué Martínez-Martínez, Olivia Brown, Mostafa Karami, and Sheida Nabavi
arxiv-2506-17133.description: Abstract Deep neural networks are increasingly being used to detect and diagnose medical conditions using medical imaging. Despite their utility, these models are highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks and distribution shifts, which can affect diagnostic reliability and undermine trust among healthcare professionals.

arxiv-2507-23593.title: Graph-based block-diagonalization of full configuration interaction Hamiltonian: H 2 chains study
arxiv-2507-23593.creator: Hayun Park, Hunpyo Lee
arxiv-2507-23593.description: Abstract We developed a graph-based block-diagonalization (GBBD) method for the full configuration interaction Hamiltonian of molecular systems to efficiently calculate the exact eigenvalues of low-energy states. In this approach, the non-zero matrix elements of the Hamiltonian are represented as edges on a graph, which naturally decomposes into disconnected clusters.

arxiv-2512-02091.title: TT-Stack: A Transformer-Based Tiered-Stacking Ensemble Framework with Meta-Learning for Automated Breast Cancer Detection in Mammography
arxiv-2512-02091.creator: 1 st Showkat Osman, 2 nd Md. Tajwar Munim Turzo, 3 rd Maher Ali Rusho *, 4 th Md. Makid Haider, 5 th Sazzadul Islam Sajin, 6 th Ayatullah Hasnat Behesti, 7 th Ahmed Faizul Haque Dhrubo, 8 th Md. Khurshid Jahan, 9 th Mohammad Abdul Qayum
arxiv-2512-02091.description: Abstract Breast cancer continues to be the second most common cause of cancer-related deaths around the world, with early detection being important to improve survival rates for patients. Traditional computer-aided diagnosis systems have limitations in their ability to represent features and generalize to the range of mammographic images.

arxiv-2604-03744.title: How Events Separated by a Timelike Interval Can Help Us Understand
arxiv-2604-03744.creator: Quantum Nonlocality

pmc-10713799.title: A novel method for the remote measurement of trismus in clinical trials using mobile phone cameras
pmc-10713799.creator: Xiang Li, Caroline Kristunas, Gabriel Landini, Annika Kroeger, Thomas Dietrich
pmc-10713799.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the reliability and validity of a novel method for remotely measuring trismus.Materials and methodsWe recruited 60 volunteers who took three types of photographs at a fixed restricted jaw position mimicking limited mouth opening, including one selfie and one portrait with or without a reference frame.

pmc-11510160.title: Applications of the Cholesterol Metabolite, 4β-Hydroxycholesterol, as a Sensitive Endogenous Biomarker for Hepatic CYP3A Activity Evaluated within a PBPK Framework
pmc-11510160.creator: Aneesh V. Karkhanis, Matthew D. Harwood, Felix Stader, Frederic Y. Bois, Sibylle Neuhoff
pmc-11510160.description: Background/Objectives: Plasma levels of 4β-hydroxycholesterol (4β-OHC), a CYP3A-specific metabolite of cholesterol, are elevated after administration of CYP3A inducers like rifampicin and carbamazepine. To simulate such plasma 4β-OHC increase, we developed a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of cholesterol and 4β-OHC in the Simcyp PBPK Simulator (Version 23, Certara UK Ltd.) using a middle-out approach.

pmc-11617375.title: Symptom clusters and network analysis in patients with gynecologic cancer undergoing chemotherapy: A cross-sectional study
pmc-11617375.creator: Jiajia Zhang, Shan Wang, Yuan Wang, Jiaru Zhuang, Ling Hang, Yibo Wu, Dewu Xu, Chunyan Huang
pmc-11617375.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to explore the complex relationships among symptoms and symptom clusters in patients with gynecologic cancer receiving chemotherapy using symptom network analysis, and to identify core symptoms and core symptom clusters.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted at the Affiliated Hospital of Jiangnan University from December 2023 to June 2024, including 221 patients with gynecologic tumors.

pmc-11710207.title: Everyday life episodic memory change and limbic quantitative PI‐2620 tau PET in participants with mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia
pmc-11710207.creator: Kittithatch Booncharoen, Akarin Hiransuthikul, Poosanu Thanapornsangsuth, Sekh Thanprasertsuk, Chanan Sukprakun, Supatporn Tepmongkol, Kammant Phanthumchinda, Yuttachai Likitjaroen
pmc-11710207.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundEpisodic memory change is among the earliest symptoms of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Accumulation of neurofibrillary tangles in limbic regions serves as a key indicator of the initial tau abnormality. This study aimed to investigate the correlations between episodic memory change and quantitative tau deposition specifically in Braak stage 3‐4 Limbic regions among participants with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and mild dementia.MethodParticipants diagnosed with MCI and mild dementia were recruited from the memory clinic at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital, Thailand.

pmc-11712595.title: Impact of AI‐based segmentation on PET analyses
pmc-11712595.creator: Luc Bracoud, Thomas Cajgfinger, Olivier Rousset, Madhura Ingalhalikar, Chris Conklin, Manja Lehmann, Joel Schaerer, David Scott, Joyce Suhy
pmc-11712595.description: BackgroundBrain MRI segmentation is required for quantitative PET analysis, in order to derive regional uptake and calculate uptake ratio relative to reference regions. FreeSurfer has been a popular method but is being supplanted by faster and more robust AI‐driven methods.

pmc-12691932.title: Enhancing Resilience and Connection: SigBee® Implementation After the Maui Wildfires
pmc-12691932.creator: Zoe Primack, Callum Chertavian, Tessa Palafu, Michelle Liu, Savannah Goshgarian-Miller, Alistair Deakin, Matt Clement, Keala Kaopuiki-Santos, Tia Hartsock, Kelsie Okamura
pmc-12691932.description: Background/Objectives: Disaster service providers responding to natural disasters face significant mental health challenges, including burnout, anxiety, and secondary trauma, which can impair both individual well-being and team functioning. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) offer scalable solutions and have demonstrated efficacy in supporting individual mental health outcomes for healthcare workers and emergency responders.

pmc-12694056.title: Deriving Motor States and Mobility Metrics from Gamified Augmented Reality Rehabilitation Exercises in People with Parkinson’s Disease
pmc-12694056.creator: Pieter F van Doorn, Edward Nyman, Koen Wishaupt, Marjolein M van der Krogt, Melvyn Roerdink, Christian Peham
pmc-12694056.description: People with Parkinson’s disease (PD) experience mobility impairments that impact daily functioning, yet conventional clinical assessments provide limited insight into real-world mobility. This study evaluated motor-state classification and the concurrent validity of mobility metrics derived from augmented-reality (AR) glasses against a markerless motion capture system (Theia3D) during gamified AR exercises.

pmc-12767255.title: Stepwise model to differentiate pathogenic from non-pathogenic organisms in urinary isolates: Effectiveness, safety, and feasibility prospective study
pmc-12767255.creator: Bimalesh Yadav, Jaideep Pilania, Ravi Kant, Balram Ji Omar, Sandeep Saini, Vikas Kumar Panwar, Yogesh Bahurupi, Prasan Kumar Panda
pmc-12767255.description: BACKGROUNDClinical decision-making in urinary tract infections depends heavily on accurately distinguishing between pathogenic and non-pathogenic organisms. The interpretation of urine culture results is influenced by proper sample collection, the patient's clinical context, and organism-specific characteristics. However, there is currently no definitive method to determine whether a urinary isolate is truly pathogenic.

pmc-12808424.title: How effective are video animations as information tools for patients and the general public? An updated systematic review
pmc-12808424.creator: Thirimon Moe-Byrne, Peter Knapp, Amber Lidster, Mim Ahamed, Hugh O'Hare, Su Golder, Jennie Lister, Joy Adamson
pmc-12808424.description: BackgroundOnline and digital communications have changed information access, with many people using the internet for health information. Our 2022 systematic review showed that video animations can improve short-term patient and public knowledge but questions remained about their longer-term effectiveness, particularly for non-native speakers and those with low health literacy, and about their effects on attitudes, cognitions (e.g., self-perceptions) and behaviour.

pmc-12821296.title: A distinct radiologic perspective on parotid pleomorphic adenoma: sialo-CBCT case report
pmc-12821296.creator: Fatma Çağlayan, Muhammed Akif Sümbüllü, Abdülkadir Şahin, Kübra Törenek Ağirman
pmc-12821296.description: BackgroundPleomorphic adenoma (PA) is the most prevalent benign salivary gland tumor, manifesting predominantly in the parotid gland. The imaging techniques most frequently employed for diagnosis include ultrasonography (USG), computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Sialography is an interventional imaging technique that utilizes a positive contrast medium to illustrate the ductal anatomy of the parotid and submandibular glands.

pmc-13367463.title: Giant Vulvar Mesonephric Duct Cysts Mimicking Malignancy: A Case Report and Diagnostic Challenge
pmc-13367463.creator: Rico Henando Sembiring, Dodi Suardi, Siti Salima, Amillia Siddiq
pmc-13367463.description: BackgroundVulvar masses present a diagnostic challenge due to their wide spectrum from benign lesions to malignancy. Mesonephric duct cysts are rare benign lesions derived from Wolffian duct remnants that may clinically mimic vulvar cancer, particularly when large or symptomatic.Case PresentationA 49-year-old multiparous woman presented with a painful vulvar mass that had progressively enlarged over one year.
